nodes.label: Orange dumbbell glyph (logo mark)
nodes.rationale: Flat single-colour, mirror-symmetric horizontal dumbbell built from rounded rectangles (thin handle bar, two tall inner plates, two shorter outer plates), no text, gradients or outlines. The dumbbell is the universal shorthand for strength training and matches the app purpose (workout, nutrition and ranking tracker); the simple shape stays legible at small launcher sizes (design intent inferred).

nodes.label: Maskable safe-zone padding
nodes.rationale: Maskable icons are cropped by the OS to a circle, squircle or rounded square, so the artwork must be opaque and full-bleed with the important content inside the centred safe zone (circle of 80 percent of the icon diameter, 205 px radius at 512 px). Here the solid #0B0F14 background fills the whole 512x512 canvas (RGB, no alpha) and the dumbbell is scaled to 0.8x of the icon-512.png version (glyph width 308 px vs 385 px; farthest glyph pixel 160 px from centre vs 200 px), leaving a safe margin so no launcher mask clips it.

nodes.label: GymTracker brand palette (#0B0F14 dark + #F97316 orange)
nodes.rationale: The icon uses exactly the app's own design tokens: background RGB(11,15,20) = #0B0F14 equals Tailwind colors.bg, the PWA manifest theme_color and background_color, and the index.html theme-color meta; glyph RGB(249,115,22) = #F97316 equals Tailwind colors.primary. The values are duplicated by hand in several places and baked into the PNG pixels rather than generated from one source, so changing the brand colour means editing all of them and regenerating the icons.

hyperedges.label: Brand palette duplicated across icon pixels, PWA manifest and Tailwind theme
